questions.question: Why is pyrrole not basic, although it contains a nitrogen atom?
options: Because the nitrogen carries no lone pair
Because the lone pair is part of the aromatic π system and protonation would destroy aromaticity
Because the N-H bond is too strong
questions.explanation: Pyrrole needs the nitrogen lone pair to reach six π electrons. Protonating the nitrogen would remove those two electrons from the ring and break the aromatic sextet, which is far too costly. Pyridine behaves differently: its lone pair sits in an sp² orbital in the ring plane and is available, hence pKa ≈ 5.2 for the conjugate acid.

questions.question: Which species satisfy the Hückel rule and are aromatic?
options: The pyrrolide anion after deprotonation of the N-H
questions.explanation: Hückel requires a planar, fully conjugated ring with 4n+2 π electrons. Pyrrole, pyridine and the pyrrolide anion all reach six. Cyclobutadiene has four, which is 4n — antiaromatic and highly unstable.

questions.question: Pyridine reacts with sodium amide at elevated temperature to give 2-aminopyridine. What is this reaction called and where does the nucleophile attack?
questions.explanation: The Chichibabin reaction is the classical nucleophilic amination of pyridine. The amide attacks C-2 because the negative charge of the resulting Meisenheimer-type adduct can be delocalised onto the ring nitrogen. Hydride leaves and hydrogen gas is evolved.

questions.question: Why is SNAr much easier on pyridine than SEAr?
options: Because the nitrogen blocks the electrophile sterically
Because SNAr does not require a leaving group
Because pyridine is electron-poor, so it welcomes nucleophiles and repels electrophiles
questions.explanation: The electronegative nitrogen withdraws π density, especially from C-2 and C-4. That deactivates the ring towards electrophiles and at the same time stabilises the anionic intermediate of a nucleophilic attack. Pyridine is therefore the mirror image of benzene chemistry.

questions.question: Bromination of furan gives predominantly which product?
questions.explanation: Like pyrrole and thiophene, furan reacts at C-2. Attack there gives three resonance structures for the arenium ion, including one in which the oxygen carries the positive charge and every atom has a full octet. Attack at C-3 offers only two.

questions.question: Order the following by increasing aromatic stabilisation (least aromatic first).
questions.explanation: Oxygen holds its lone pair most tightly, so furan delocalises least and behaves partly like a diene — it undergoes Diels-Alder reactions. Pyrrole donates better, thiophene better still because sulfur is large and polarisable. Benzene remains the reference at the top.

questions.question: Histidine acts as an acid-base catalyst in many enzymes. Which property of its imidazole ring makes that possible?
options: The N-H is strongly acidic with pKa 2.5
The pyridine-type nitrogen has a pKa around 7, so both protonated and free forms exist at physiological pH
Imidazole is not aromatic and therefore flexible
The ring binds metal ions irreversibly
questions.explanation: A catalyst that has to accept and release a proton must be half protonated at working pH. With pKa ≈ 7 the imidazole of histidine sits exactly at physiological pH, which is why it appears in serine proteases and carbonic anhydrase.

questions.question: Which pair of starting materials gives an isoxazole by [3+2] cycloaddition?
questions.explanation: The nitrile oxide R–C≡N⁺–O⁻ is the 1,3-dipole that carries both the nitrogen and the oxygen into the new ring, giving an isoxazole with an alkyne and an isoxazoline with an alkene. Azide plus alkyne would give a triazole, diazoalkane plus alkene a pyrazoline, tetrazine plus enamine a pyridazine after loss of N₂.

questions.question: Which statements about cyclocondensations are correct?
options: Unsymmetrical components can give two regioisomers
The reaction is always concerted and passes through no intermediate
A small molecule such as water or ammonia is lost during ring closure
The steps are nucleophilic and electrophilic, not pericyclic
questions.explanation: Cyclocondensation is ordinary carbonyl chemistry run twice: attack, dehydration, ring closure, dehydration. Because it proceeds through discrete intermediates, unsymmetrical partners can combine in two ways — which is precisely why pre-formed enamines are used to fix the regiochemistry. Only cycloadditions are concerted.

questions.question: The Biginelli reaction combines which three components?
questions.explanation: The Biginelli three-component reaction gives dihydropyrimidinones from an aldehyde, a β-ketoester and urea in one pot. It belongs to the same family as the Hantzsch dihydropyridine synthesis, which replaces urea with ammonia and gives a dihydropyridine instead.

questions.question: Indole is brominated. Where does the electrophile attack and why?
options: At C-3, because the arenium ion then leaves the benzene ring aromatic
At C-2, because that position is closest to nitrogen
At C-5 of the benzene ring, because it is most electron-rich
At nitrogen, because it carries the lone pair
questions.explanation: Indole is the standard exception to the C-2 rule of five-membered heteroaromatics. Attack at C-3 lets the positive charge rest on nitrogen while the fused benzene ring keeps its own aromatic sextet. Attack at C-2 would have to delocalise the charge into the benzene ring and break it.

questions.question: Which statements about the Kondrat'eva pyridine synthesis are correct?
options: The reaction requires a palladium catalyst
CO₂ is lost in the retro-[4+2] step
questions.explanation: Kondrat'eva is a thermal cycloaddition followed by a retro-cycloaddition. The oxazole supplies four π electrons, the alkyne two, and the bridged intermediate fragments with loss of carbon dioxide to give the aromatic pyridine. No transition metal is involved.

questions.question: In the Paal-Knorr pyrrole synthesis, what is the final driving force for the last tautomerisation?
options: Formation of the aromatic pyrrole ring
questions.explanation: The last step converts the non-aromatic dihydropyrrole into the aromatic ring. Aromatic stabilisation is what makes the whole condensation sequence run to completion; the two dehydration steps before it are individually reversible.

questions.question: A lead compound carrying a carboxylic acid shows poor membrane permeability and rapid conjugation. Which replacement is the classical first choice?
options: Replace COOH by a methyl group
questions.explanation: Tetrazole keeps the acidity (pKa 4 to 5) and the hydrogen-bonding pattern that the target recognises, but resists glucuronidation and is somewhat more lipophilic. Removing the acid or swapping it for a methyl group would drop the key interaction; an aldehyde is reactive and metabolically unstable.
